gbm_population_flag.reason: Eligibility names 'high-grade primary glial brain tumor (WHO grade III and IV)'; grade IV glioma without IDH is read as historical glioblastoma (D27C), giving mixed_glioma_gbm_named, but glioblastoma itself is named only in an exclusion (recurrent GBM) and the description, so high_grade_glioma_unspecified is possible.

candidate_evidence.quote: For the maintenance phase of anesthesia, patients in the propofol group will receive continuous infusions of propofol and remifentanil.

With this background, it seems propofol based anesthesia may limit the progression of brain cancer progression and therefore, the purpose is to evaluate type of anesthetics (propofol versus sevoflurane) as a factor responsible for glioma progression and survival characteristics.

coder_notes: Feasibility RCT (Phase NA) of propofol TIVA vs sevoflurane maintenance anaesthesia during primary glioma craniotomy, with a stated antitumour hypothesis for propofol, so propofol is a candidate (rule 2 exception). Propofol is also given as an induction bolus in both arms; the candidate row refers to propofol maintenance infusion in the Propofol group. Sevoflurane only in the ACTIVE_COMPARATOR arm (control_comparator). Remifentanil, fentanyl and rocuronium given in both arms as anaesthesia (supportive). Population is suspected WHO grade III-IV glioma; see gbm_population flag. Regimen coded monotherapy because no other antitumour drug or radiotherapy is part of the experimental arm intervention (postoperative chemo/radiotherapy only recorded as follow-up data). Rocuronium moiety given as INN 'rocuronium bromide'; the script may normalise to rocuronium.
